title: Istanbul Airport (IST) vs Sabiha Gökçen (SAW): Transfers & Timing
seoTitle: IST vs SAW Airport Transfer Guide (2026 Times & Costs)
metaDescription: Compare Istanbul Airport (IST) and Sabiha Gökçen (SAW) in 2026: M11 and M4 metro times, Havaist fares, private transfers, and check-in buffers.
quickAnswer: Istanbul Airport (IST) sits 40 km northwest of central Europe-side hotels and takes 45–75 minutes by car or 30–37 minutes by M11 metro to Gayrettepe. Sabiha Gökçen (SAW) serves the Asian side, reaching Kadıköy in 50 minutes on the M4 metro or Taksim in 60–95 minutes depending on Bosphorus bridge traffic.

body.text: How long does the transfer take from IST and SAW?

Plan for 45 to 75 minutes by road from Istanbul Airport (IST) to Sultanahmet, Karaköy, or Nişantaşı, and 60 to 95 minutes from Sabiha Gökçen (SAW) to European-side hotels. Rail cuts traffic risk sharply: the [M11 metro](https://www.istairport.com/en/airport/airport-transportation/urban-transportation/public-transportation?locale=en) reaches Gayrettepe in 30–37 minutes, while the [M4 metro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M4_(Istanbul_Metro)) reaches Kadıköy from SAW in about 50 minutes.

Weekday rush hours (07:30–10:00 and 16:30–20:00) and rainy Friday evenings add 30 to 45 minutes to Bosphorus bridge crossings. Factor in terminal exit time too: walking from a far IST arrival gate through passport control to curbside pickup routinely takes 45 to 60 minutes.
Should you take a private transfer, Havaist or metro?

Pick the metro for predictable timing during rush hour, [Havaist](https://www.hava.ist/sefer-saatleri.php?lang=en) or [Havabüs](https://www.havabus.com/) for single-seat budget travel with checked luggage, and a pre-booked private transfer when arriving after 22:00, travelling with two or more people, or staying on Sultanahmet's cobbled side streets.

The M11 metro extended to Halkalı on 20 June 2026 ([Istanbul Airport](https://www.istairport.com/en/airport/airport-transportation/urban-transportation/public-transportation?locale=en)), yet reaching Sultanahmet still requires transferring at Gayrettepe to M2. At SAW, the M4 sits beneath the terminal and runs every five to six minutes daytime ([Royal Ride](https://www.royalrideturkey.com/en/blog/istanbul-airport-and-sabiha-gokcen-metro-guide-m11-and-m4)).

items: Choose a private transfer if: Two or more travellers split the fixed van fee, you carry heavy bags, or you land overnight when metros close (roughly 00:00–06:00).
Choose Havaist / Havabüs if: You travel solo and stay near Taksim, Sultanahmet (HVL-13), or Kadıköy piers.
Ignore terminal touts: Skip unofficial drivers offering "VIP taxis"; pre-book licensed vans or use official metered ranks.

body.text: Which airport is better for Asian-side or European-side hotels?

Always match your airport to your hotel's continent when fares are similar. IST serves European-side neighbourhoods—Sultanahmet, Karaköy, Nişantaşı, and Beşiktaş—without a Bosphorus crossing, while SAW sits on the Asian side, cutting transfers to Kadıköy, Moda, and Üsküdar nearly in half.

A €35 cheaper SAW ticket rarely pays off if you stay in Sultanahmet: a cross-Bosphorus van in afternoon traffic costs €60–€90 and eats two hours. Conversely, guests basing themselves in Kadıköy—see our [where to stay in Istanbul guide](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/blog/where-to-stay-in-istanbul) and [Asian side of Istanbul guide](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/blog/asian-side-istanbul-guide)—reach their hotel faster from SAW via M4.
How early must you arrive for international flights?

Arrive at the terminal at least three hours before international departures from IST and two and a half to three hours before international departures from SAW. [Turkish Airlines](https://www.turkishairlines.com/en-tr/istanbul-airport/faq/) explicitly recommends three hours for international flights and two hours for domestic flights at IST.

Two quirks catch visitors off guard: both airports enforce double security screening (first at the terminal entrance door, then airside after passport control per [IST Check-in Guide](https://www.istairport.com/en/services/discover/airport-facilities/check-in-counters?locale=en)), and walking to outer IST gates takes 15 to 20 minutes. Leave European-side hotels four to four and a half hours ahead during rush hour, and add thirty minutes if crossing from Asia.

faq.q: Can I pay for the M11 or M4 airport metro with a contactless credit card?
faq.a: Contactless foreign cards work on select turnstiles at a higher single-ride rate, but reliability varies by bank. Buying and loading a physical Istanbulkart at the yellow ticket machines outside the metro gates takes three minutes and also covers trams, ferries, and the Marmaray.

faq.q: Do Havaist and Havabüs airport shuttles run 24 hours a day?
faq.a: Major Havaist lines from IST, including Taksim and Sultanahmet, operate round the clock with reduced overnight frequency every 45 to 60 minutes. Havabüs from SAW to Taksim runs roughly 06:30 to 01:30, so late-night SAW arrivals should pre-book a private transfer or metered taxi.

faq.q: How much does a taxi cost from Istanbul Airport (IST) to Sultanahmet?
faq.a: Expect roughly ₺1,800 to ₺2,400 (€35–€48) on the official yellow taxi meter in normal traffic, plus highway tolls if used. Always confirm the meter is switched on before leaving the rank and keep small Turkish lira notes or a card ready for payment.

faq.q: Is the M11 metro station directly inside Istanbul Airport terminal?
faq.a: No—unlike SAW's integrated station, the M11 metro sits across a covered pedestrian walkway about 300 metres from the IST arrivals exit. Follow the red "M" signs from Arrivals Level -2; the walk takes six to ten minutes with rolling luggage.

faq.q: How long should I leave for an IST-to-SAW airport connection?
faq.a: Allow at least five to six hours between scheduled landing and next departure. The two airports sit roughly 85 km apart across the Bosphorus, requiring baggage claim, immigration, a 90-to-130-minute road transfer, and fresh check-in plus double security screening.

faq.q: Can I take a ferry from either Istanbul airport?
faq.a: Neither airport has a ferry pier. However, SAW travellers can ride the M4 metro to Kadıköy pier in 50 minutes and board a 20-minute Şehir Hatları ferry to Karaköy or Eminönü—a scenic, traffic-proof option if you are carrying light luggage.
